questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: The map in registers.map above, 32-bit word registers at byte offsets 0x00 to 0x3C
questions.reason: The request names the readouts but gives no offsets, so the proposed map is a guess.
questions.answer:
BUSY: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [0] a packet is part-way
CTR_GOOD..CTR_PROTO: offset 0x10, RO, reset 0: 0x10 good, 0x11 bad check, 0x12 short, 0x13 long, 0x14 repeat, 0x15 stale, 0x16 type or length; 16 bits, wrapping
LASTSEQ: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] last accepted number, [16] one once a packet was accepted
SEQ: offset 0x03, RO, reset 0: sequence number of the last good packet
PAY0: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: first two payload bytes of the last good packet, big-endian, zero filled
BYTE: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag; reads the last 9 bits written
PAY1: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: next four payload bytes, big-endian, zero filled when a good packet has fewer
TYPE: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: type of the last good packet
RESULT: offset 0x01, RO, reset 0: class of the last packet: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: any offset not listed reads as 0 and ignores writes, as do the read-only registers
questions.evidence: BUSY: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [0] a packet is part-way

questions.text: What are the values of CLKS_PER_BIT, TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: 100 MHz / 115200 is 868; the others are not given.
questions.answer: CLKS_PER_BIT is 868, which matches the proposed default. TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not the proposed 1000000. BUILD_STAMP is not specified.

questions.text: Should not-new keep separate counters for repeat and out-of-order?
questions.default: No, one not-new counter covers both
questions.reason: The request asks for one counter per class and lists not new as one class.
questions.answer: Yes. The specification gives repeat and stale their own counters, 0x14 for repeat and 0x15 for stale. The proposed single not-new counter is not in the spec.
questions.evidence: Counters 0x10 good, 0x11 bad check, 0x12 short, 0x13 long, 0x14 repeat, 0x15 stale, 0x16 protocol (type and length), 16-bit wrapping.

questions.text: What is the numeric code of each class in the result register?
questions.default: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length
questions.reason: The request orders the classes but gives no encoding.
questions.answer: Yes. The RESULT register codes are: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length.
